subject: geography
title: Megacities and Urban Growth
welcome_lead: Step into Tokyo, Delhi, Shanghai and Lagos — cities of more than 10 million reshaping the planet.
meta_desc: Geography Adventure: megacities, urban hierarchies and global urban growth.
final_note: You have walked through the world's biggest urban agglomerations. Their fortunes will shape the 21st century.

concepts.def: Urban agglomeration with more than 10 million inhabitants.
Urban region exceeding 20 million inhabitants, e.g. Tokyo, Delhi.
Ordering of settlements by population and function.
City disproportionately larger than the next in a national urban system, e.g. Bangkok.
City exerting global influence through finance, culture and politics, e.g. New York, London, Tokyo.
Movement of population from cities to smaller settlements and rural areas, observed in some HICs.

walkthroughs.body_html: Globally there are more than 30 megacities, the largest including Tokyo, Delhi, Shanghai, São Paulo, Mexico City, Cairo, Mumbai, Beijing, Dhaka and Osaka. The UN projects over 40 megacities by 2030, with most growth in Asia and Africa.

Urban hierarchies range from balanced (Germany) to highly primate (Thailand, Argentina, Peru). Global cities — New York, London, Tokyo, Hong Kong, Paris, Singapore — concentrate corporate headquarters, financial services and cultural infrastructure.

Rural-urban migration, natural increase and economic agglomeration drive megacity growth. Pull factors include jobs, services and education; push factors include rural poverty and climate stress. Cities provide opportunity but also concentrate inequality and environmental risk.
